surprises.description: BRX reported Q3 Nareit FFO of $0.60 per share, $0.01 above the preview’s roughly $0.59 consensus estimate. That is a modest beat, rather than the expected in-line quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 NAREIT FFO grew over 7% year-over-year to $0.60 per share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Nareit FFO / diluted share | Q3 FY2026 Consensus | ~$0.59.”

surprises.description: Same-property NOI growth was 6.6%, above the preview’s expected 5.0%–5.5% range. The result also came in above the preview’s stated 5.0%+ threshold for exceeding the implied H2 run rate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Same property NOI increased 6.6% in the quarter (driven by a 480 basis point contribution from base rent).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Same-property NOI growth | ~5.0–5.5% (implied)” and “A Q3 SP NOI print of 5.0%+ runs above the implied H2 run-rate.”

surprises.description: The full-year FFO guide rose to $2.36–$2.38 per share. The preview expected a likely narrowing to $2.36–$2.37, so BRX’s new high end was a cent above that anticipated outcome.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised its full-year FFO guidance to $2.36-$2.38 per share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The most likely action is a narrowing to $2.36–$2.37.”

surprises.description: Total leased occupancy reached 95.6%, well ahead of the preview’s 95.0% threshold and its 95.0%–95.1% base-case range. This delivered a stronger H2 recovery signal than the preview’s expected minimum inflection.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total leased occupancy reached a record 95.6%, up 80 basis points sequentially and 150 basis points year-over-year.”

surprises.description: Leasing spreads were stronger than the preview’s expected deceleration: new-lease spreads were 43% rather than merely holding above the 25% concern threshold, while blended spreads were 25% versus the prior 19.1% reference point. Renewal spreads also exceeded the preview’s prior 15.5% figure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Blended comparable rent spread of 25%, with new lease spreads of 43% (anchors above 70%) and renewal spreads exceeding 19%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “New-lease spreads below ~25% would challenge the below-market-rent thesis”; the preview cited Q2 spreads of “31.3% new / 15.5% renewal / 19.1% blended” and described them as “lumpy and decelerating.”

surprises.description: BRX raised the lower end of its full-year same-property NOI outlook from 5.00% to 5.5%, while keeping the upper end at 5.75%. The increase was more limited than a full-range raise, but stronger than the preview’s expectation that the guide might simply narrow.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year same property NOI guidance was raised to 5.5%-5.75% growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed existing FY26 guidance of “5.00%–5.75%” and said “The most likely action is a narrowing to $2.36–$2.37” for FFO, describing a guidance raise as mostly priced.

surprises.description: The SNO pipeline’s expected commencements were larger than the preview’s cited estimates: about $55 million of rent is expected to commence in 2026 versus roughly $29 million anticipated for H2, and another $48 million in 2027 versus roughly $37 million expected in 2027+. This points to a stronger near-term conversion bridge than the preview described.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The signed-but-not-yet-commenced pipeline ended at $69 million, with ~$55 million of rent expected to commence in 2026 and another $48 million in 2027 before additional leasing.”

surprises.description: The board raised the quarterly dividend by more than 7%, an increase the preview did not flag as an expected announcement. Management tied the raise to visibility into continued earnings and cash flow growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The board increased the quarterly dividend by more than 7%, reflecting management's visibility into continued earnings and cash flow growth.”

surprises.description: BRX provided a concrete debt-financing step for Slate by arranging a $400 million delayed-draw term loan and $400 million of forward-starting swaps. However, the facts provided do not quantify Slate accretion or establish that the full financing plan avoids equity, leaving the central funding and dilution questions only partly addressed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company is arranging a $400 million delayed draw term loan plus $400 million of forward-starting swaps to fund the Slate acquisition expected to close in Q1 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified whether management “clarifies permanent financing and the equity-issuance risk” as a key issue and asked for “Slate accretion, quantified.”
